- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.67 and recent highs are followed by model overshoots).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or drops below 0.35, especially after a recent peak.
- Reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% if sentiment history shows a sharp decline or negative sentiment in the last 3–5 days.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment volatility; model should not adjust more than 3–5% per day unless sentiment is extreme.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is consistently high (>0.8) and price is trending up, model should not over-forecast beyond 15% above recent peak.
- For 30-day horizon, reduce forecast by 2–5% if sentiment is low or mixed (0.2–0.6) and price has been trending down.
- Do not assume sentiment directly translates to price; model should adjust for sentiment lag (e.g., 2–3 day delay in price reaction).
